In Chamber Case :- CRIMINAL APPEAL No. - 4554 of 2024 Appellant :- Lalit Kumar Bajpai Respondent :- State Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Appellant :- Aditya Yadav,Pawan Kumar Dubey,Shivam Yadav Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Sunil Vashisth Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
Heard Sri Shivam Yadav, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Sunil Vashisth, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2, Sri Ratnesh Nandan Singh, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against the bail rejection order dated 02.04.2024 passed by learned Special Judge (SC/ST Act)/Additional Sessions Judge, Ghaziabad in Bail Application No. 1790 of 2024 (Lalit Kumar Bajpai vs. State of U.P.) arising out of Case Crime No. 35 of 2024, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC and sections 3(2)(v), 3(s) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Masuri, District Ghaziabad.

sentences.text: It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant and the prosecutrix were posted at District Jail, Ghaziabad.
The appellant being a Senior Police Officer was a Trainee Instructor of the prosecutrix who was a newly appointed Jail Warden.
The prosecutrix, in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., has stated that she is a married lady and had estranged relationship with her husband Sushil Kumar.

During her training period as Jail Warden,
she was called to the house of the appellant and was served with a cold drink and became unconscious.
Though she realised of having forceful physical relation with the appellant but she could not resist and found herself in an uncomfortable position.

Subsequently, some obscene photographs and videos were shown to the prosecutrix and was threatened to be viraled, therefore,
the physical relations were continued for almost two years.
Learned counsel for the appellant has asserted that no photographs or the videos have been produced by the prosecutrix nor the alleged incident took place within the public view.
It has also been stated that the prosecutrix refused to undergo the medical examination.
The allegations are concocted and false and unbelievable.
The appellant is languishing in jail since 07.03.2024 and there is no criminal history against the appellant except the present case.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.
Learned counsel for the opposite parties have vehemently opposed the aforesaid submissions but could not dispute the aforesaid facts.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, let the appellant-Lalit Kumar Bajpai involved in Case Crime No. 35 of 2024, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC and sections 3(2)(v), 3(s) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Masuri, District Ghaziabad be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.
